newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-AAMODT MAKES IT TWO FOR NORWAY'S MEN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-AAMODT MAKES IT TWO FOR NORWAY'S MEN.

text.p: Norway's Kjetil-Andre Aamodt collected the fourth gold medal of his career on Thursday when he won the men's combined at the Alpine skiing world championships.

The former Olympic super-giant slalom champion and 1993 world slalom and giant slalom champion clocked a total time of three minutes 10.40 seconds over the two- race event comprising a downhill and slalom.
It was Norway's second gold of the championships in just two men's events raced so far.
Switzerland's Bruno Kernen was second in 3:10.68 while Austria's Mario Reiter took bronze in 3:11.69.

Overall World Cup leader Aamodt had been third after the first leg of the slalom, raced under floodlights on the Kandahar piste, and he must have thought he was destined for a lower position on the podium.
More than half a second in front of him had been Lasse Kjus, the compatriot who beat him into second place in the combined in both the 1994 Olympics and the 1993 world championships.
But Kjus, who won silver in the opening super-G on Monday, made several mistakes in the second leg and finished fifth.
The 1996 world champion, Marc Girardelli of Luxembourg, who has not competed since December due to injury, did not defend his title due to injury.
